blocks.title: Core Concepts : Tissue System
blocks.text:
• The study of the internal structure of plants is called anatomy.
  • The internal structure of plant organs also shows variations.
  • Monocots and dicots are also seen to be anatomically different.
  • Internal structure also shows adaptation to diverse environments.
EPIDERMAL TISSUE SYSTEM :

Epidermis:

  • Outermost protective covering of primary plant body, Usually single layered, Parenchymatous
  • Cells have large central vacuole
Cuticle:

  • Waxy layer outside epidermis
  • Prevents water loss from transpiration
  • Absent in roots
Stomata:

  • Present in leaves usually
  • Regulate gaseous exchange and transpiration
  • Guard cells regulate opening and closing of stomata
Stomatal apparatus: Guard cells + Subsidiary cells + Stomatal aperture

Root hair: Unicellular, Absorption of water and minerals

Stem hair/Trichomes:

  • Usually multicellular, may be branched or unbranched and soft or stiff, sometimes secretory.
  • Prevent water loss due to transpiration.

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
• Mistaking it as a single layer; some plants have multiple epidermal layers.
  • Believing it is only for protection, ignoring roles like water regulation and gas exchange.
  • Thinking all stomata are open at the same time; stomatal opening is regulated by environmental factors.
  • Assuming they are present only on the upper surface of leaves; in many plants, they are more abundant on the lower surface.
  • Assuming all plants have a thick cuticle; its thickness varies based on habitat.
  • Believing the cuticle is permeable; it is waterproof and reduces water loss.

blocks.title: Question.1
blocks.question:
Stomata in grass leaf are

(1) Dumb-bell shaped

(2) Kidney shaped

(3) Rectangular

(4) Barrel shaped
blocks.answer:
Ans= 1

Explanation

In grasses and other monocots, the guard cells of stomata are dumb-bell shaped. This shape is an adaptation to their function:

  • Guard cells in grass have narrow middle regions and broader ends, resembling a dumb-bell.
  • This structure allows efficient opening and closing of the stomatal pore to regulate gas exchange and water loss.

blocks.title: Core Concepts: Ground & Vascular
blocks.text:
GROUND TISSUE SYSTEM

  • All tissues except the epidermis and vascular bundle form ground tissue
  • Major part of plant organ
  • Consists of Simple permanent tissues (such as parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma)
  • Ground tissue system of leaf: Mesophyll

blocks.title: Vascular Tissue System
blocks.text:
• Conducting tissue
  • Xylem and phloem
  • Water, mineral and food conduction

blocks.title: Question 1 : Ground
blocks.question:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : Endarch and exarch are the terms often used for describing the position of secondary xylem in the plant body.

Statement II : Exarch condition is the most common feature of the root system.

In the light of the above statements, choose  the correct answer from the options given below;

(1) Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

(2) Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.

(3) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.

(4) Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
blocks.answer:
Answer (3)

Statement I is incorrect because endarch and exarch are terms used to describe the development and arrangement of primary xylem in plant vascular tissue, not secondary xylem.

Statement II is correct because exarch condition is indeed the most common feature of the root system, where the xylem develops towards the outer part of the root, with the phloem inside. This is characteristic of many plants, especially in roots.
options: (1) Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
(2) Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
(3) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
(4) Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

blocks.title: Question 2: Ground
blocks.question:
Which of the following is not a part of the ground tissue system?

(1) Mesophyll cells

(2) Trichomes

(3) Companion cells

(4) Subsidiary cells
blocks.answer:
Answer - 3

The stomatal apparatus consists of the following components:

  • Mesophyll cells - In leaves, the ground tissue consists of thin- walled chloroplast containing cells and is called mesophyll.
  • Trichome - On the stem the epidermal hairs are called trichomes. The trichomes in the shoot system are usually multicellular. Trichomes are part of the ground tissue system.
  • Companion Cells - Not a part of the ground tissue system. Companion cells are elements of phloem of angiosperm. It is a part of the vascular tissue system.
  • Subsidiary cells: Additional cells that support the guard cells and help in their function, usually found in some plants.

modules.name: Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants

blocks.title: Question 1
blocks.question:
The transverse section of a plant part showed polyarch, radial and exarch xylem, with endodermis and pericycle. The plant part is identified as :

(1) Monocot root

(2) Dicot root

(3) Dicot stem

(4) Monocot stem
blocks.answer:
Answer (1)

  • Polyarch xylem refers to the condition where there are many xylem bundles, which is typical of a monocot root.
  • Radial xylem means the xylem and phloem are arranged alternately in a circle, a characteristic of roots.
  • Exarch xylem means the xylem matures from the outside towards the center, a condition found in roots of many plants, particularly monocots.
  • Endodermis and pericycle are also present in roots, with the endodermis surrounding the vascular tissue and the pericycle giving rise to lateral roots.
blocks.prompt: The transverse section of a plant part showed polyarch, radial and exarch xylem, with endodermis and pericycle. The plant part is identified as :

blocks.title: Question 2
blocks.question:
In a dicot root, the pericycle gives rise to:

(1) Lateral roots

(2) Cork cambium

(3) A portion of vascular cambium

(4) All of the above
blocks.answer:
Answer (4)

In a dicot root, the pericycle is the layer of cells just inside the endodermis and surrounding the vascular tissue. It has multiple functions:

  • Lateral roots: The pericycle is primarily responsible for giving rise to lateral roots. These roots emerge through the cortex and epidermis.
  • Cork cambium: In the case of secondary growth, the pericycle can give rise to cork cambium, which forms the outer protective layer (cork) during secondary growth.
  • Vascular cambium: The pericycle can also contribute to the formation of vascular cambium, which is responsible for the secondary growth in the vascular tissue of the root.

blocks.title: Question 3
blocks.question:
The transverse section of a plant shows following anatomical features:

(a) Large number of scattered vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath.

(b) Large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue.

(c) Vascular bundles conjoint and closed.

(d) Phloem parenchyma absent.

Identify the category of plant and its part :-

(1) Dicotyledonous root

(2) Monocotyledonous stem

(3) Monocotyledonous root

(4) Dicotyledonous stem
blocks.answer:
Answer (2)

The anatomical features described in the question match the typical characteristics of a monocotyledonous stem.

blocks.title: Question 4
blocks.question:
Read A to D and tell the correct order of components from the outer side to the inner side in a young dicot stem.

(A) Cortex

(B) Pericycle

(C) Epidermis

(D)  Pith

(1) C, D, B, A       (2) A, B, C, D

(3) C, A, B, D       (4) C, B, A, D
blocks.answer:
Answer (3)

In a young dicot stem, the correct order of components from the outermost to innermost side is as follows:

  • C (Epidermis): The outermost protective layer.
  • A (Cortex): Beneath the epidermis, a region of parenchymatous cells that stores food and provides support.
  • B (Pericycle): Located just inside the cortex, the pericycle gives rise to lateral roots and may also contribute to the formation of vascular cambium.
  • D (Pith): The innermost region of the stem, primarily made up of parenchymatous cells involved in storage and transport.
Thus, the correct order is C, A, B, D.
blocks.prompt: Read A to D and tell the correct order of components from the outer side to the inner side in a young dicot stem.

blocks.title: Question 5
blocks.question:
Large, empty colourless cells of the adaxial epidermis along the veins of grass leaves are:

(1) Lenticels

(2) Guard cells

(3) Bundle sheath cells

(4) Bulliform cells
blocks.answer:
Answer (4)

Bulliform cells are large, empty, colorless cells found in the adaxial epidermis of grass leaves, particularly along the veins. These cells play a crucial role in regulating leaf movement. They are involved in the process of leaf folding during water stress, helping reduce water loss by closing the leaf surface.
